verdict_basis: One MED finding (R31-01): the r031 acceptance program fails its own generator --check against the qualified source, and its six closure check ids do not appear in the qualification receipt. The product itself reproduces exactly: custody exact; replay 453/455 on 3.12.3 and 3.13.16 with only the two known environment non-passes and test-id set equal to the receipt; release and cold boot rebuild byte-identical; transtemporal archive verifies independently and reconstructs the r031 runtime byte for byte; C11 verifier compiles warning-free and passes on the exact tree. findings.title: The r031 acceptance program does not bind the qualified source or the qualification receipt
evidence: tools/build_transtemporal_r031_program.py --check exits 1 with R031_PROGRAM_DRIFT:SOURCE-DENOMINATOR.json on both interpreters.

Two of its 15 denominator files changed after sealing: tests/test_transtemporal_archive.py (81420b7e.../7167 B -> 355c0ec5.../7496 B) and tools/build_transtemporal_r031_operator_kit.py (60b49a72.../5880 B -> 2cba4204.../5881 B). Both are in the qualified source (root 603b6e4d...).

All six R31 work selections name closure ids with a 'tests.' prefix (e.g. tests.test_transtemporal_archive.TranstemporalArchiveTests.test_two_revisions_...); the receipt lists these tests only without it. The other 125 selections use the receipt's form. pippi_work_units never resolves a closure id against a receipt, and no qualification test runs the current program's --check, so neither defect is caught.
The r028 and r029 program --check both passed in their own revisions.
findings.impact: The R31-01..06 acceptance records cannot be shown, by exact identity, to close on the qualified bytes. The underlying tests exist and pass in replay under their bare ids, so this is an evidence-binding defect, not a product defect.
findings.repair: Regenerate the r031 program after the final source edit, using the receipt's test-id form; add a qualification test that runs the current revision's program --check and requires every direct_closure_check_id to appear in the receipt.
findings.escalation_note: Rated MED by the R24-01 precedent (generated record stale against shipped source). LOW if program records are not a required leg.

findings.impact: Your PASS (court root 738b9f8b...) was produced by a court that cannot be rebuilt from the released source. The repair itself is correct, minimal and honestly declared.

findings.title: The C11 verifier has no denominator: it passes whatever rows its manifest lists
findings.evidence: The line protocol carries no row count and no binding to the manifest root, and the verifier does not check ROOT for unlisted files. By source, a header-only manifest returns PASS with checked 0, and a truncated one passes on its remaining rows. The doc says it checks SHA-256 'for every file'. Not executed (no negative exercises, per instruction).
findings.mitigation: The doc scopes it as a narrow projection, and the Python reference verifier remains mandatory; the printed checked count is the only signal.
findings.repair: Add a trailer line with file count and manifest_root (or a digest of the rows) and refuse checked==0 or a count mismatch; optionally flag files under ROOT not listed.
